$comment: Read by scripts/audit-claims.mjs over dist/**/*.html, dist/**/*.xml, JSON-LD and alt text, and (version 3) over dist/**/*.txt and dist/**/*.md as plain text with link addresses removed (llms.txt, llms-full.txt, robots.txt and the Markdown twins); a data-claim-allow marker cannot exempt a plain-text file. A required rule with ifBuilt true skips a listed route that is not built, so a wave 7 page is held to the rule from the day it exists; a listed route may be a text file such as /llms.txt. Classes follow SAGE-PLAN 3.2 (C-06 to C-17, C-24). The package names Spark, Launch, Accelerate and Studio are allowed (owner decision 2026-10-09, C-10); the seat price literal is added by the operator when flags change, and numbers are never recorded here. Investor Introductions is allowed as a flat-fee add-on (C-14), and the rules block only success-based, commission and guarantee wording. Four sections: `rules` (unconditional; the source-level unit tests in tests/unit also apply these to the repository, so add a rule here only when no source file matches it), `contextRules` (wording that is legitimate in a few named places; applied to the built output only), `required` (text that must be present on the listed `routes`, on every page whose <main> text matches `whenMatches`, or only when `when` holds; `whenFlags` sets the regex flags of `whenMatches`, default "i") and `manifestRules` (checks on src/assets/photo/manifest.json). A context rule can carry `disabledByFlag` (inactive while that flag in src/data/flags.ts is on), `allowPaths` (route regexes where it does not apply), `markerAllowed` (elements marked data-claim-allow="<rule id>" or "*" are skipped) and `genericDefinitionAllowed` (elements marked data-generic-definition are skipped).

rules.description: A currency amount tied to a seat or monthly rate
An investor network. WE offers curated, limited introductions as a paid add-on; it does not claim a network of investors
A promise of meetings, introductions or investor contact. A negation such as "cannot promise a meeting" or "no guarantee of meetings" passes
A years-of-experience claim (FLAG-YEARS; the registry shows the entity filed in 2022)
Specific security controls asserted as practice
Agreement title is not for public pages

contextRules.description: Public benefit corporation wording while FLAG-PBC (pbcWording) is off

Success-based, contingent, commission, carried-interest or equity pay for investor introductions. Investor Introductions is a flat fee that does not depend on any investment closing. The audit scans built output only; add data-claim-allow="C-14-success-based" to an element that must quote the wording in order to deny it
"Fundable" stated as an outcome WE delivers (WE promises no funding). "Fundability" and a question such as "will this make my company fundable?" do not match

Implied peer group, staff or alumni while none exist. Allowed on the FAQ, which answers "is WE an accelerator?", on the metrics definitions page, where "cohort" is an analytics term, on the one comparison page whose subject is the word accelerator (its Markdown twin is the same route; DP-W8-15), and in llms.txt and llms-full.txt, which restate the FAQ sentence that this site does not describe a cohort calendar or a demo day and cannot carry a data-claim-allow marker (plain text)

First-person peer, mentor, cohort or accelerator wording: "our cohort", "WE mentors", "WE runs a cohort". WE has none of these (C-13), so the sentence is false whoever wrote it, and no data-claim-allow marker can exempt it, even in the one place the generic word is allowed. A denial ("WE has no mentors") does not match
The phrase is permitted on the dedicated-teams page only

A "no fee" claim about the commercial model (amounts are unpublished and the model is under counsel review). The one legitimate use is the verbatim Investor Introductions disclaimer, "takes no fee or stake tied to any investment", which the lookahead exempts
A no-equity claim about the commercial model. The Investor Introductions disclaimer says "no fee or stake" and does not match
A free-of-charge claim about the commercial model
A response-time or decision-time promise. WE publishes no timeline for replies or decisions (DP-5: a timeline needs an operator source)
A count of applications or an acceptance rate. WE has no published figures, and a number here would be an unsourced social-proof claim
A seat count tied to a named package. The packages are sized by stage and depth only; no seat count is published per package (F-4, C-06, C-10)
UK spelling; the site uses US spelling (a Delaware company)
The company is "WE" in capitals, not the pronoun "We", in sentences about what it does
